title: Read the build frontier beside the acceptance frontier on greg path, and place the 2026-10-30 correction on N1
problem: At feb531d2, greg path stops at N1 in every container. N1 moves only on a closure signed at the founder tier, and the founder's 2026-10-30 correction puts the device run at the end of the build ('That is done when we completely build the prompt'). So how much of the prompt is built could only be claimed in prose, which is the inflation the directive forbids. Reproduced on feb531d2: greg/path.py has no build_status, `greg path --build` exits with 'greg: error: unrecognized arguments: --build', and the first 11-test unit file fails 10 of 11.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261028-OPUS-MAXIMUS-REISSUE (sections 12, 14, 15, 16, 57, 68 and 70, as mapped in the unit plan WU-01)
INTENT-2026-09-30-DEVELOPMENTAL-INHERITANCE (placement with the nine-question test; exactly one operationally primary node)
baseline: feb531d2: greg/path.py position() walks the path at the founder tier and reports achieved, active and met_ahead. Each predicate already computes structurally_met through _tiered(). greg/cli.py has `greg path` and `greg path --node`. There is no build view, no mutation gate for the path predicates, and the correction is recorded in the intent ledger but not on greg/path.json or as a placement.

alternatives.name: Proposed: build_status beside position(), guarded by a live-mutant read and a gate that runs exactly that read
alternatives.description: greg/path.py build_status(journal) gives each node STRUCTURALLY_BUILT, BUILD_OPEN or NO_PREDICATE from the predicates' own structurally_met. It reports the build frontier (first node not built), the acceptance frontier (position()'s active node, with a status derived from its build state), achieved unchanged, built_ahead (reported, never counted) and structural_depth (consecutive built nodes that are mutation-guarded). mutation_guarded() reads the gate's MUTANTS with ast.literal_eval and counts only live mutants. scripts/ci/check_path_predicate_mutants.py runs exactly that read (33 mutants). `greg path --build` prints it. greg/path.json gains the intent id and `rehearsal` refs; the placement n1.vepmc_is_final_acceptance_not_build_gate is appended.
advantages: Build progress is read from the body's own ledger, not claimed in prose
position() output is unchanged and stays the one operationally primary node; a reviewer probe found plain `greg path` and `greg path --node N3` byte-identical between feb531d2 and the reviewed head
Every node predicate and the frontier rule have at least one weakening mutant, all 33 caught
Uses mechanisms already in the tree: _tiered structurally_met, the founder tier, the existing mutant-gate pattern
disadvantages: The gate is not in CI, so mutation_guarded shows a mutant is listed and live, not that it is caught
One weakening per predicate is not exhaustive
structural_depth reaches only 2 on one body driven through the CLI
alternatives.revival_evidence: Retained; revisit when the gate is wired into canonical-ci.yml or when the N5 and N8 predicates land.

alternatives.name: Simplest viable: build_status from structurally_met alone
alternatives.description: The unit plan's first sketch without the guard: a node is built when its predicate is structurally met, and the build frontier is the first node that is not. No mutation_guarded, no structural_depth, no gate.
advantages: Smallest change: one function and one CLI flag
disadvantages: A weakened predicate would raise the build count silently; the first plan critique noted that N4, N6 and N7 then had no mutant, so they could read as built while the build-phase counting rule says they cannot count
No instrument to stop a later PR from loosening a predicate
alternatives.revival_evidence: If every predicate is permanently guarded by a gate that runs in CI, the per-node guard could be reduced to a CI badge.

alternatives.name: Strongest competing design: a gate-written receipt, keyed to source hashes, that mutation_guarded requires
alternatives.description: The gate writes a receipt naming the source hashes it ran against; mutation_guarded counts a node only when a receipt for the current greg/path.py and named tests shows its mutant caught.
advantages: Shows caught, not only listed and live
Closes the scenario where a live mutant names a test that cannot catch it
disadvantages: Every edit to greg/path.py or to a named test, by any PR, drops structural_depth to 0 until the gate is re-run
A receipt in the tree is one more artifact to keep in step on every branch
Wiring the gate into CI gives the same assurance per head at lower cost
alternatives.revival_evidence: Revive if the gate cannot be wired into canonical-ci.yml, or if a merged head shows a guarded node whose mutant survives a gate run.

alternatives.name: Staged and reversible: a read-only view first, then CI wiring, then the missing predicates
alternatives.description: Land build_status and `greg path --build` as a draft child PR stacked on #227. The #196 integrator then wires the gate into canonical-ci.yml. WU-02 rehearses the whole path on one body; WU-04 and WU-06 add the N5 and N8 predicates; WU-08 tightens N3. Each later PR adds its own mutant and rehearsal ref.
advantages: Each step is separately reviewable and revertible
Avoids canonical-ci.yml, which is hot on other open PRs
The view writes nothing, so reverting it loses no data
disadvantages: Until the gate is wired, a catch is shown only where someone runs the gate
The build frontier cannot pass N5 until its predicate exists
alternatives.revival_evidence: Adopted as the delivery sequence of the proposed design; revisit if the integrator cannot wire the gate into canonical-ci.yml.

pass_2.attack_summary: Two review rounds, each by two separate agents of this same session, attacked the strengthened design: whether the guard certifies itself, whether a malformed gate crashes the view, whether the status overstates, whether an invalid mutant can count as caught, whether the static read can disagree with what the gate runs, whether structural evidence can move the founder's path, and whether the records overclaim.

new_weaknesses.statement: mutation_guarded certified itself: a stale or no-op mutant kept its node guarded and counted in structural_depth (round 1, WU01-F1)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: A mutant guards only while live: its text occurs exactly once, its replacement differs, and its named test is one pytest would collect

new_weaknesses.statement: MUTANTS = None, 5 or {[1]: 2} raised TypeError out of `greg path --build` (round 1, WU01-F3)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: A literal that is not a list, or is malformed, reads as nothing; the CLI exits 0; two mutants pin it

new_weaknesses.statement: The acceptance status said 'final step' even for an unbuilt or unmeasurable node (round 1, WU01-F2)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The status follows the node's build state: pending only when built, 'build open; acceptance follows the build' or 'no ledger predicate yet; cannot be accepted' otherwise

new_weaknesses.statement: The repository-node rule had no test or mutant, and one unit assertion on founder_tier_count was vacuous (round 1)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: A test and a caught mutant for the repository rule; the vacuous assertion removed; the real founder_tier_count assertion lives in the integration rehearsal

new_weaknesses.statement: The gate counted a mutant that broke a lazily imported module as caught (round 2, WU01-ATK-1)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: A mutated Python file must import under its dotted name before its test runs; a test failing on SyntaxError, ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError is INVALID; two mutants pin it

new_weaknesses.statement: The static read could disagree with what the gate runs or counts: a re-bound list, an off-target mutant, a docstring 'test' (round 2, WU01-ATK-2)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The list is read only when bound once and named nowhere else, and the gate runs exactly that read; a node-tagged mutant must sit in its predicate's span; tests are found by AST as pytest collects them; ten mutants pin it

new_weaknesses.statement: The implementer's report went stale against the branch it described (round 2, WU01-FID-1)
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The report was regenerated from the evidence README, and the PR text is built from the README

new_weaknesses.statement: The gate takes about 167-197 s per run
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Kept out of canonical-ci.yml in this PR; the integrator decides where it runs

pass_2.final_design: build_status beside position(), sharing _walk; STRUCTURALLY_BUILT, BUILD_OPEN or NO_PREDICATE per node from structurally_met; the build frontier stops at the first unbuilt or unmeasurable node; the acceptance frontier is position()'s active node with a status derived from its build; achieved unchanged; built_ahead reported, never counted; structural_depth counts consecutive built nodes guarded by a live mutant; mutation_guarded reads MUTANTS statically, only when bound once, with predicate-span targeting and AST test lookup; the gate runs exactly that read, imports each mutated file first and refuses import-error catches; `greg path --build` exclusive with --node; path.json gains the intent id and rehearsal refs (shape-checked only); one appended N1 placement.
